title: Pushing the Boundaries of AI Chips: From Monolithic 3D CMOS to Cryogenic Computing
problem: CMOS scaling approaches fundamental limits while AI and LLM workloads demand unprecedented compute performance and memory bandwidth, creating bottlenecks in current computing architectures.
motivation: Explosive growth of AI/LLM applications reveals critical performance and efficiency bottlenecks in conventional 2D CMOS chip design, necessitating paradigm shifts in physical device and system architecture.
method: Presents two complementary paradigms: (1) 3D monolithic CMOS integration using Complementary FETs (CFETs) with vertically stacked pMOS/nMOS transistors and memory layers integrated atop logic; (2) cryogenic temperature operation of chips where transistors achieve enhanced performance and reduced parasitic resistance.
key_novelty: Monolithic 3D CMOS architecture combining vertically stacked CFETs and on-logic memory stacking for unprecedented density and on-chip memory capacity.
contributions: 3D monolithic CMOS integration strategy leveraging CFET vertical stacking for logic density
Memory-on-logic integration paradigm for expanded on-chip capacity
Cryogenic computing approach demonstrating performance and power benefits

metrics.other: logic density, on-chip memory capacity, performance per watt

limitations: No quantitative performance/efficiency metrics provided; cryogenic infrastructure costs and practical deployment challenges not discussed.
primary_theme: 3D monolithic and cryogenic paradigms for AI computing
